title: The Currency-Plus-Commodity Basket: A Proposal for Exchange Rates in Oil-Exporting Countries to Accommodate Trade Shocks Automatically
venue: Institutions and Macroeconomic Policy in Resource-Rich Arab Economies, edited by Kamiar Mohaddes, Jeffrey Nugent and Hoda Selim (Oxford University Press: Oxford, UK), Chapter 6, pp. 149-182
abstract: This chapter proposes an exchange rate regime for oil-exporting countries, designed to deliver monetary policy that accommodates rather than exacerbates the effects of oil market swings, yet offers the transparency and predictability of a currency peg. The proposal is called currency-plus-commodity basket (CCB). The plan is to peg the national currency to a basket that includes not only the currencies of major trading partners but also the export commodity (oil). The chapter provides evidence from six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries that times when their currencies were “undervalued” relative to the CCB alternative were periods of overheating, as reflected in high inflation, and external imbalance, as reflected in high balance-of-payments surpluses. Conversely, periods when the currencies were “overvalued” featured unusually low inflation and low balance of payments. This suggests the economy would have been more stable under CCB. Finally, the chapter offers a practical blueprint for implementation of the proposal.
abstract_zh: 本章为石油出口国提出了一种汇率制度，旨在使货币政策能够适应而非加剧石油市场波动的影响，同时又具备货币钉住制度的透明度与可预测性。该方案被称为货币加商品篮子（CCB）。其计划是将本国货币钉住一个篮子，该篮子不仅包括主要贸易伙伴的货币，还包括出口商品（石油）。本章利用六个海湾合作委员会（GCC）国家的证据表明，其货币相对于CCB替代方案被“低估”的时期，正是经济过热的时期，表现为高通胀；同时也是对外失衡的时期，表现为国际收支大幅顺差。反之，货币被“高估”的时期则伴随着异常低的通胀和较低的国际收支水平。这表明，在CCB制度下经济本会更加稳定。最后，本章提供了该方案的一份实用实施蓝图。

title: Sustainable Cooperation in Global Climate Policy: Specific Formulas and Emission Targets
venue: Climate Change Economics, vol.5, no.3, August
abstract: We propose a framework that, building on the pledges made by governments after the Copenhagen Accord of 2009, could be used to assign allocations of emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs), across all countries, one budget period at a time, as envisioned at the 2011 negotiations in Durban. Under this two-part plan: (i) China, India, and other developing countries accept targets at Business as Usual (BAU) in the coming budget period, the same period in which the U.S. first agrees to cuts below BAU; and (ii) all countries are asked in the future to make further cuts in accordance with a common numerical formula that each country is likely to view as fair. We use a state of the art integrated assessment model to project economic and environmental effects of the computed emission targets.

title: The Natural Resource Curse: A Survey
venue: Ch. 1 in Beyond the Resource Curse, edited by Brenda Shaffer (University of Pennsylvania Press), 2012, pp. 17-57
abstract: It is striking how often countries with oil or other natural resource wealth have failed to grow more rapidly than those without. This is the phenomenon known as the Natural Resource Curse. The principle has been borne out in some econometric tests of the determinants of economic performance across a comprehensive sample of countries. This paper considers six aspects of commodity wealth, each of interest in its own right, but each also a channel that some have suggested could lead to sub-standard economic performance. They are: long-term trends in world commodity prices, volatility, crowding out of manufacturing, civil war, poor institutions, and the Dutch Disease. Skeptics have questioned the Natural Resource Curse, pointing to examples of commodity-exporting countries that have done well and arguing that resource endowments and booms are not exogenous. The paper concludes with a consideration of institutions and policies that some commodity-producers have tried, in efforts to overcome the pitfalls of the Curse. Ideas include indexation of oil contracts, hedging of export proceeds, denomination of debt in terms of oil, Chile-style fiscal rules, a monetary target that emphasizes product prices, transparent commodity funds, and lump-sum distribution.
abstract_zh: 拥有石油或其他自然资源财富的国家，其经济增长往往未能快于那些没有此类财富的国家，这一现象颇为引人注目。这一现象被称为自然资源诅咒。在一些针对全面国家样本的经济绩效决定因素的计量检验中，这一原理得到了证实。本文考察了商品财富的六个方面，每一方面本身都值得关注，但同时也都是有人提出的可能导致经济绩效不佳的渠道。它们是：世界商品价格的长期趋势、价格波动、对制造业的挤出、内战、制度低下以及荷兰病。怀疑论者对自然资源诅咒提出了质疑，指出一些商品出口国表现良好的例子，并认为资源禀赋和繁荣并非外生的。本文最后考察了一些商品生产国为克服诅咒的陷阱而尝试过的制度与政策，包括：石油合同指数化、出口收入套期保值、以石油计价的债务、智利式财政规则、强调产品价格的货币目标、透明的商品基金以及一次性分配。

title: The Natural Resource Curse: A Survey of Diagnoses and Some Prescriptions
venue: in Commodity Price Volatility and Inclusive Growth in Low-Income Countries, edited by Rabah Arezki, Catherine Pattillo, Marc Quintyn and Min Zhu (International Monetary Fund), 2012
abstract: Countries with oil, mineral or other natural resource wealth, on average, have failed to show better economic performance than those without, often because of undesirable side effects. This is the phenomenon known as the Natural Resource Curse. This paper reviews the literature, classified according to six channels of causation that have been proposed. The possible channels are: (i) long-term trends in world prices, (ii) price volatility, (iii) permanent crowding out of manufacturing, (iv) autocratic/oligarchic institutions, (v) anarchic institutions, and (vi) cyclical Dutch Disease. With the exception of the first channel--the long-term trend in commodity prices does not appear to be downward--each of the other channels is an important part of the phenomenon. Skeptics have questioned the Natural Resource Curse, pointing to examples of commodity-exporting countries that have done well and arguing that resource exports and booms are not exogenous. The relevant policy question for a country with natural resources is how to make the best of them.
abstract_zh: 拥有石油、矿产或其他自然资源财富的国家，平均而言，其经济表现并未优于没有这些财富的国家，这往往是由于一些不良的副作用所致。这一现象被称为自然资源诅咒。本文按照所提出的六种因果渠道对文献进行分类回顾。这些可能的渠道包括：(i) 世界价格的长期趋势，(ii) 价格波动，(iii) 对制造业的永久性挤出，(iv) 专制/寡头制度，(v) 无政府制度，以及 (vi) 周期性荷兰病。除第一种渠道之外——商品价格的长期趋势似乎并非下降——其他每一种渠道都是该现象的重要组成部分。怀疑论者对自然资源诅咒提出了质疑，指出一些商品出口国表现良好的例子，并认为资源出口和繁荣并非外生的。对于拥有自然资源的国家而言，相关的政策问题是如何最大限度地利用这些资源。

title: Determinants of Agricultural and Mineral Commodity Prices
venue: Chapter 1 in Inflation in an Era of Relative Price Shocks (Reserve Bank of Australia: Sydney), 2010: pp. 9-51
abstract: Prices of most agricultural and mineral commodities rose strongly in the past decade, peaking sharply in 2008. Popular explanations included strong global growth (especially from China and India), easy monetary policy (as reflected in low real interest rates or expected inflation), a speculative bubble (resulting from bandwagon expectations) and risk (possibly resulting from geopolitical uncertainties). Motivated in part by this episode, this paper presents a theory that allows a role for macroeconomic determinants of real commodity prices, along the lines of the "overshooting" model: the resulting model includes global GDP and the real interest rate as macroeconomic factors. Our model also includes microeconomic determinants; we include inventory levels, measures of uncertainty, and the spot-forward spread. We estimate the equation in a variety of different ways, for eleven individual commodities. Although two macroeconomic fundamentals--global output and inflation--both have positive effects on real commodity prices, the fundamentals that seem to have the most consistent and strongest effects are microeconomic variables: volatility, inventories, and the spot-forward spread. There is also some evidence of a bandwagon effect.
abstract_zh: 过去十年间，大多数农产品和矿产品价格大幅上涨，并于2008年急剧达到峰值。流行的解释包括：强劲的全球增长（尤其是来自中国和印度的增长）、宽松的货币政策（体现为低实际利率或预期通胀）、投机泡沫（源于随大流的预期）以及风险（可能源于地缘政治不确定性）。受此次事件的部分启发，本文提出了一种理论，允许宏观经济因素对实际商品价格发挥作用，其思路类似于“超调”模型：由此得到的模型包括全球GDP和实际利率作为宏观经济因素。我们的模型还包括微观经济决定因素；我们纳入了库存水平、不确定性指标以及现货—远期价差。我们以多种不同方式对11种单一商品估计了该方程。尽管两个宏观基本面——全球产出和通胀——都对实际商品价格有正向影响，但看起来影响最为一致且最强的基本面却是微观经济变量：波动率、库存以及现货—远期价差。也有一些证据表明存在随大流效应。

title: An Elaborated Proposal For Global Climate Policy Architecture: Specific Formulas and Emission Targets for All Countries in All Decades
venue: Chapter 2, in Post-Kyoto International Climate Policy, edited by Joe Aldy and Rob Stavins (Cambridge University Press), 2009, pp.31-87. HPICA Disc.Paper 08-08
abstract: This paper analyzes a detailed plan to set quantitative national limits on emissions of greenhouse gases, following along the lines of the Kyoto Protocol. It is designed to fill in the most serious gaps: the absence of targets extending as far as 2100, the absence of participation by the United States and developing countries, and the absence of reason to think that countries will abide by commitments. The plan elaborates on the idea of a framework of formulas that can assign quantitative limits across countries, one budget period at a time. Unlike other century-long paths of emission targets that are based purely on science (concentration goals) or ethics (equal rights per capita) or economics (cost-benefit optimization), this plan is based partly on politics. Three political constraints are particularly important.(1) Developing countries are not asked to bear any cost in the early years.(2) Thereafter, they are not asked to make any sacrifice that is different in kind or degree than was made by those countries that went before them, with due allowance for differences in incomes.(3) No country is asked to accept an ex ante target that costs it more than, say, 1% of GDP in present value, or more than, say, 5% of GDP in any single budget period. They would not agree to ex ante targets that turned out to have such high costs, nor abide by them ex post. An announced target path that implies a future violation of these constraints will not be credible, and thus will not provide the necessary signals to firms today. The idea is that (i) China and other developing countries are asked to accept targets at BAU in the coming budget period, the same in which the US first agrees to cuts below BAU; and (ii) all countries are asked to make further cuts in the future in accordance with a formula which sums up a Progressive Reductions Factor, a Latecomer Catch-up Factor, and a Gradual Equalization Factor. The paper tries out specific values for the parameters in the formulas (parameters that govern the extent of progressivity and equity, and the speed with which latecomers must eventually catch up).The resulting target paths for emissions are run through the WITCH model. It does turn out to be possible to achieve the carbon abatement goal (concentrations of 500 PPM in 2100) while simultaneously obeying the economic/political constraint (no country suffers a disproportionate loss in GDP).Preliminary efforts to achieve a target of 450 ppm have so far been unable to do so without violating the cost constraint.
abstract_zh: 本文分析了一项详细方案，该方案沿袭《京都议定书》的思路，为各国温室气体排放设定定量限额。其设计旨在弥补最严重的缺口：目标未延伸至2100年、美国和发展中国家未参与，以及没有理由认为各国会遵守承诺。该方案阐发了一个公式框架的理念，即可以按预算期逐期为各国分配定量限额。与其他纯粹基于科学（浓度目标）、伦理（人均平等权利）或经济学（成本效益优化）的百年排放目标路径不同，本方案部分地基于政治。其中三项政治约束尤为重要。（1）早期不要求发展中国家承担任何成本。（2）此后，不要求它们做出在种类或程度上不同于先行国家所作出的牺牲，并适当考虑收入差异。（3）不要求任何国家接受事前目标，使其在现值上的成本超过例如GDP的1%，或在任何单一预算期内超过GDP的5%。各国不会同意那些事后被证明成本如此之高的事前目标，也不会在事后遵守这些目标。一个宣布的目标路径如果意味着未来将违反这些约束，就不可信，因而无法向今天的企业提供必要的信号。其思路是：(i) 要求中国和其他发展中国家在即将到来的预算期内接受BAU下的目标，这与美国首次同意削减至BAU以下的预算期相同；(ii) 要求所有国家此后依据一个公式进行进一步削减，该公式汇总了渐进减排因子、后来者追赶因子以及逐步均等化因子。本文为公式中的参数（即决定累进性和公平程度，以及后来者最终必须追赶的速度的参数）尝试了具体取值。由此得出的排放目标路径通过WITCH模型运行。结果表明，既能够实现碳减排目标（2100年浓度达到500 ppm），又能同时遵守经济/政治约束（没有任何国家的GDP遭受不成比例的损失），这是可以做到的。关于实现450 ppm目标的初步尝试，至今未能在不违反成本约束的情况下做到这一点。

title: Formulas for Quantitative Emission Targets
venue: Chapter 2 in Architectures for Agreement: Addressing Global Climate Change in the Post Kyoto World, edited by Joe Aldy and Robert Stavins (Cambridge University Press), 2007, pp. 32-56
abstract: Start from three premises: (1) Global Climate Change is a genuine problem; (2) the Kyoto Protocol constitutes the only multilateral framework we have to address it; and (3) the Protocol is inadequate, particularly with regard to incomplete coverage across countries (no participation of US or developing countries) and across time (nothing agreed after 2012). This paper argues that - given the combination of political, economic and scientific realities as they are - Kyoto is a good foundation, a good first stepping stone on the most practical path if we are to address Climate Change seriously. A constructive approach asks what are the requirements for the design of a second step in the process, a successor to the Kyoto regime of 2008-2012, one that would build on what is good about it and fix what is most lacking. This paper offers a proposal that seeks realistically to bring in all countries and to look far into the future. It argues that the path of emission targets for the 21st century must be selected sequentially, perhaps one decade at a time, all within a common framework. An analogy for the framework would be the post-war General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which gave us 50 years of successful rounds negotiating trade liberalization, even though the original signers did know what specifics would emerge. The paper proposes allocating relative targets across countries by means of a formula that is fairly general at first but that becomes increasingly specific as the decade in question approaches. New joiners would be obligated to adopt emissions targets, but these paths need not immediately fall below their "business as usual" growth path. Allowing new joiners to sell permits in the initial budget period would then provide them with an economic incentive to join, or at least would not penalize them. It would carry economic benefits for both rich and poor countries, while also bringing environmental benefits to all. Countries would be required in subsequent budget periods of their participation to adopt steeper reductions in their emissions targets relative to their "business as usual" paths. The extent of relative cuts across countries would depend on such factors in the formulas as the per capita income and past emission levels of the country in question. The extent of cuts in aggregate global emissions would depend - as is inevitable - on how strong is the international political consensus for aggressive action at that point in history. Such a scheme provides the necessary flexibility and incentives to appeal to both industrialized and developing countries.
abstract_zh: 从三个前提出发：(1) 全球气候变化是一个真实存在的问题；(2) 《京都议定书》是我们应对这一问题所拥有的唯一多边框架；(3) 该议定书存在不足，尤其是在国家覆盖范围（美国和发展中国家未参与）和时间覆盖范围（2012年之后未达成任何协议）方面。本文认为，鉴于当前的政治、经济和科学现实，京都机制是一个良好的基础，是如果我们要认真应对气候变化，在最务实的路径上迈出的一个良好的第一步。一种建设性的思路是，询问设计第二步——即2008至2012年京都机制的后继机制——需要满足哪些要求，这一机制应当在京都机制的优点基础上，弥补其最为欠缺之处。本文提出了一项方案，力求现实地纳入所有国家，并着眼于遥远的未来。文章认为，21世纪的排放目标路径必须按顺序选定，或许每次一个十年，且都在一个共同框架之内完成。该框架的类比对象是战后的《关税与贸易总协定》（GATT），它使我们在50年间通过一轮轮谈判取得了成功的贸易自由化，尽管最初的签署方并不知道具体将会产生什么内容。本文提出，通过一个公式在各国之间分配相对目标，该公式起初较为笼统，但随着相关十年的临近而变得越来越具体。新加入的国家应有义务采纳排放目标，但这些路径不必立即低于其“一切照常”的增长路径。允许新加入者在最初的预算期内出售排放许可，将为其提供加入的经济激励，或至少不会对其造成惩罚。这将为富国和穷国都带来经济效益，同时也将为所有国家带来环境效益。各国在其参与的后续预算期内，将被要求相对于其“一切照常”路径，采取更为陡峭的排放目标削减。各国之间的相对削减幅度将取决于公式中的某些因素，例如相关国家的人均收入和过去的排放水平。全球总排放的削减幅度则不可避免地取决于在那一历史时刻，国际政治上对采取积极行动的共识有多强。这样的方案为吸引发达国家和发展中国家提供了必要的灵活性与激励。

title: Globalization and the Environment
venue: in Globalization: What’s New, edited by Michael Weinstein,(Columbia University Press: NY), 2005, pp. 129-169
abstract: Fears that globalization necessarily hurts the environment are not well-founded.A survey reveals little statistical evidence, on average across countries, that openness to international trade undermines national attempts at environmental regulation through a "race to the bottom" effect. If anything, favorable "gains from trade" effects dominate on average, for measures of air pollution such as SO 2 concentrations. Perceptions that WTO panel rulings have interfered with the ability of individual countries to pursue environmental goals are also poorly informed. Recent rulings have in fact confirmed that countries can enact environmental measures, even if they affect trade and even if they concern others' Processes and Production Methods (PPMs), provided the measures do not discriminate among producer countries. People care about both the environment and the economy. As real incomes rise, their demand for environmental quality rises. This translates into environmental progress under the right conditions --democracy, effective regulation, and externalities that are largely confined within national borders and are therefore amenable to national regulation. Increasingly, however, environmental problems spill across borders. Global externalities include climate change and ozone depletion. Economic growth alone will not address such problems, in a system where each country acts individually, due to the free rider problem. Multilateral institutions are needed, and national sovereignty is the obstacle, not the other way around.
abstract_zh: 认为全球化必然损害环境的担忧缺乏充分依据。一项调查显示，平均而言，跨国数据中几乎没有统计证据表明，国际贸易的开放会通过“逐底竞争”效应削弱各国的环境监管尝试。若有的话，就二氧化硫浓度等空气污染指标而言，有利的“贸易收益”效应平均占据主导。人们认为世界贸易组织（WTO）专家组裁决干扰了各国追求环境目标能力的看法，同样缺乏充分依据。事实上，近期的裁决已确认，各国可以颁布环境措施，即使这些措施影响贸易，甚至即使它们涉及他国的生产工艺与生产方法（PPMs），只要这些措施不在生产国之间进行歧视。人们既关心环境，也关心经济。随着实际收入的提高，他们对环境质量的需求也随之上升。在适当的条件下——民主制度、有效的监管，以及大体限于国界之内、因而适于国内监管的外部性——这将转化为环境进步。然而，环境问题日益跨越国界。全球性外部性包括气候变化和臭氧层破坏。在各国各自行动的体系中，由于搭便车问题，仅靠经济增长无法解决此类问题。需要多边机构，而障碍在于国家主权，而非相反。

title: Is Trade Good or Bad for the Environment? Sorting Out the Causality
venue: Review of Economics and Statistics, 87, no. 1, Feb. 2005, 85-91
abstract: What is the effect of trade on a country's environment, for a given level of GDP?Some have observed an apparent positive correlation between openness to trade and measures of environmental quality. But this could be due to endogeneity of trade, rather than causality. This paper uses exogenous determinants of trade -geographical variables from the gravity model -as instruments to isolate the effect of openness. The finding is that trade may indeed have a beneficial effect on three measures of air pollution. Statistical significance is lacking for Particulate Matter, but is moderate for NO2, and high for SO2.Results for broader environmental measures are not as encouraging, but one can at least say that there is little evidence that trade has the detrimental effect on the environment that the race-to-the-bottom theory would lead one to expect. The larger effect appears to come via income itself: our results generally support the environmental Kuznets curve, which says that growth harms the environment at low levels of income and helps at high levels, and to support the proposition that openness to trade accelerates the growth process.
abstract_zh: 在给定的GDP水平下，贸易对一国环境的影响是什么？有人观察到贸易开放程度与环境质量指标之间存在明显的正相关关系。但这可能是由于贸易的内生性，而非因果关系所致。本文利用贸易的外生决定因素——引力模型中的地理变量——作为工具变量，以分离出开放程度的效应。研究发现，贸易确实可能对三项空气污染指标产生有益影响。颗粒物的结果缺乏统计显著性，二氧化氮的结果显著性中等，而二氧化硫的结果显著性较高。更广泛的环境指标结果则不那么令人鼓舞，但至少可以说，几乎没有证据表明贸易对环境产生了逐底竞争理论所预期的那种有害影响。更大的效应似乎是通过收入本身产生的：我们的结果总体上支持环境库兹涅茨曲线，即增长在收入水平较低时损害环境，而在收入水平较高时则有益于环境；并且支持贸易开放加速增长进程这一命题。
